messages:
ryan: seeing surge of Xid errors on eu-central1-rack9 starting ~07:10UTC. inference p95 jumped from 220ms -> 2.6s. Looks correlated with a few GPU resets. anyone around? :warning:

infra-bot: alert triggered: gpu.xid_count > threshold on cluster eu-central1-rack9 (since 2026-03-17T07:09Z). Incident ID: INC-20260317-045.

maya: on it. which nodes? can we isolate quickly and drain?

jon: quick dump from node-eu9-3 (GPU3):
```
dmesg | tail -n 6
NVRM: Xid (13) at 0x00007f13 00000000 0x00000004
NVRM: GPU reset failed: -2
kernel: watchdog: gpu-reset triggered
```
`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` shows ECC correctable: 124, uncorrectable: 3 on GPU3.

sam: starting drain of node-eu9-3 now - `kubectl drain node-eu9-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` - moving pods off.

maya: also labeling it quarantine: `kubectl label node node-eu9-3 redwood/gpu-status=quarantine --overwrite` :white_check_mark:

ops-oncall: routing change: adding fallback policy to direct new inference traffic for model 'redwood-small' away from eu-central1 to us-west2 for 30m. will monitor p95 across regions.

jon: firmware/driver logs: `NVRM: Xid (13) 00000000 0x00000004` repeats ~every 10-30s before reset. Also saw 12V rail sag recorded in sensor stream at 07:08:12Z on pmic0: voltage dropped ~11% for ~6s. possible PSU/rail instability.

sre-runbook-bot: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-power-thermal - follow "Xid + PSU sag" checklist (PSU rails, reseat card, RMA if persisting).

ryan: if rail sag is real, we should check datacenter ops/maintenance windows. @ops-oncall did we have any scheduled work around 07:00?

ops-oncall: no scheduled maintenance. I've paged colo NOC to check for power feed blips.

maya: short-term mitigation: lowering power cap to 200W on affected GPUs to avoid hitting reset condition: `nvidia-smi -i 3 -pl 200` applied to node-eu9-3 GPU3.

jon: after lowering power cap, Xid frequency dropped significantly over 10m but not zero. tail latency improved ~20% from peak. still seeing some redispatches.

sam: spun up 8 extra instances in us-west2 and scaled the dedicated pool. traffic shifted, current overall p95 back to ~300ms. cost impact estimate if kept for 24h: ~$2.7k.

jon: I've also scheduled a hardware swap for rack9-slot4 (vendor RMA). will capture ECC counters pre-swap and post-swap.

ryan: good. action items: (1) finish node drain + quarantine (maya/sam) (2) monitor ECC/Xid counts for 1h (jon) (3) colo NOC follow up re: rail sag (ops-oncall) (4) RMA + replace card (jon) (5) if ignition again, escalate to full rack replacement.

maya: executed (1) and (2) started. adding log collection snippet to thread: `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 200 > /tmp/gpu-node-eu9-3-journal.log`

ops-oncall: colo NOC confirms transient PD (phase imbalance) on feeder B at 07:05-07:12, they restarted redundant PSU at 07:13. they will follow up with a ticket.

jon: post-PSU restart, Xid events tapered off on other nodes too. looks like the root cause is likely the transient power event. still going ahead with RMA to be safe.

ryan: agree. once RMA completes and we see 1h clean, we'll close. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam: replacing card in rack9-slot4 now. will post status.

sre-runbook-bot: note: long-term recommendations appended in runbook: deploy chassis-level PMIC monitoring, add automatic node fencing on repeated Xid, and consider soft-power-cap policies to auto-mitigate during rail instability.

jon: FYI, I pushed a short-term scheduler change to avoid tight colocations of critical inference pods on nodes with rising ECC counts - `kube-scheduler` patch applied.

ryan: updating incident log INC-20260317-045 with the actions and cost numbers. closing criteria: no Xid for 1h and node back in pool.

sam: replaced card done. ECC counters reset baseline. monitoring for 40m.

maya: 40m in, no Xid on node-eu9-3, metrics look stable. moving to unquarantine and `kubectl uncordon node-eu9-3`.

ryan: unquarantine + rejoin. closing after one more 20m quiet. thanks all.
